group.name: Encryption tool
group.str: Help - scroll the text with the mouse wheel.
Key Token Tool - for encrypted mod packs
A token (CNEK1-...) is the key rewritten as different text: hand it to players instead of the key.\nThey paste it into the prompt that opens an encrypted mod pack.
Enhanced: CNE container (CNEZ, needs the key)

Enhanced: the zip is wrapped in a CNEZ container. No archive tool can open it at all - only\nCodename Engine can, with the key (or a token). Safest option, but nobody can browse the mod in\n7-Zip and every tool that expects a real zip just sees garbage.

Standard: the zip stays a normal zip, but every entry is encrypted with AES-256 (WinZip AES).\n7-Zip, WinRAR and Bandizip open it with the password, and so does the engine - players are asked\nfor that password at startup. Hand out the key or a token: the same password works in both.

Pick one protection mode first - it is required, exactly one of the two. The engine reads .hxb
transparently, so a protected script is a drop in replacement for the .hx it came from - same name,
different extension. Key mode also keeps a copy of the source, so Decrypt can turn the file back
into .hx. VM mode only stores bytecode, so the game runs it but Decrypt has nothing to write out.
Key encryption - ChaCha20 + HMAC tag, needs the key (source can be restored)
VM bytecode - compiled, with a per file opcode permutation (bytecode only)
Extra layers - optional, they stack on the mode above:
Byte offset - the whole payload rotated by N bits
Split - cut into pieces, shuffled, padding in between
The source travels inside the file, so Decrypt can restore it.
Bytecode only, so Decrypt cannot write the source back out.

WHAT THIS TOOL DOES

The Mod Pack tab seals a zip mod into a CNEZ container or an AES-256 password zip, unwraps
either one into a plain zip again, and turns keys into shareable tokens. The Scripts tab
seals a single script into a .hxb the engine keeps loading like a .hx.

keys

The key is whatever sits in the Key field of the token tool. Empty means: the key
script_key.txt (next to the executable or in the mod folder) has for that pack name, or the
built-in engine key. A custom key must also be in script_key.txt, or the engine cannot open
the pack again. File > Reload Key File re-reads it without a restart. script_key.txt holds
either one key on its first line, or one "name = key" per line, where name is a file name,
a name without extension, a mod relative path, or * as fallback; # and // start a comment.

key tokens: a token (CNEK1-...) is the key rewritten as different text. Players paste it
into the prompt that opens an encrypted zip mod. Copy Key / Copy Token put either one on
the clipboard.

mod pack formats

 CNEZ container: only the engine can open it, the key is required.
 AES-256 zip: 7-Zip, WinRAR and Bandizip open it with the password, and so does the
 engine, so players only type the password once.

the Scripts tab

Pick one or more .hx files, pick a protection mode, switch on any extra layer you want and
it writes name_protected.hxb next to the source. The engine loads .hxb like any other
script, so the .hx can be deleted afterwards and the protected file takes its place.

 protection mode - required, exactly one of the two:
 key encryption: ChaCha20 plus an HMAC tag, the same key rules as above. The payload
 is the source, so Decrypt can turn the file back into .hx.
 VM bytecode: compiled with a per file random opcode permutation, so a disassembly of
 one script does not describe the next. Compiling drops the source text, so the file
 runs but Decrypt has nothing to write out.

 extra layers - optional, they stack on the mode above:
 byte offset: the payload is rotated by N bits, which stops a plain file signature.
 split: the payload is cut into pieces, shuffled, with random padding in between.
 Both are pure byte shuffles: the numbers needed to undo them sit in the plain header,
 so they never keep a file from being restored.

Why a mode and not both: the source copy is only ever embedded when it is encrypted as
well (an unencrypted copy would be readable straight out of the file), and a VM pack has
no key to seal it with. So: key mode is the restorable one, VM mode is the one that only
the game can read.

Encrypting and decrypting both run in the background with a progress bar and write a new
file next to the source: name_encrypted.zip, name_password.zip or name_decrypted.zip.
Plain zips load as before; password zips from other tools load too (ZipCrypto, AES-128/192/
256) - the password is asked at startup and the readable copy stays in the hidden
.cne/keys folder, which is deleted when the game closes.
